text:
clarence: Kicking off an Inverra Systems POC. They want streaming chat + tool/function calls, deterministic JSON output (strict schema), SAML SSO, and customer-managed KMS (BYOK). POC will be hosted but they want ephemeral browser creds and an explicit plan for token rotation. Also asked for a burst cost estimate: ~1k QPS for 10-25m.

maya: Quick clarifications: 1) browser clients or server-side connectors? 2) do they require resumable streams on reconnect?

clarence: Both. Shopfront is browser SSE for low-latency UX; backend enrichment workers are server-side. They do want resumable on reconnect so product pages don't lose context.

tom: Tech notes: current SDKs (js/python) support streaming + function calls. Browser: SSE/EventSource is simplest; server: websocket recommended. Function calls are emitted as stream chunks with type=\"function_call\" and args as JSON string. For deterministic output, send a JSON Schema in the system prompt and validate client-side when the assembled object completes.

priya: Security: Hosted+BYOK is supported on enterprise plans but requires LOA + KMS attestation and legal signoff. SOC2 can be shared under NDA. If they need HSM-backed keys or special retention for audit logs, that adds time/cost.

maya: Edge case: ephemeral creds + SSE can hit a mid-stream rotation problem: if token rotates and client retries aggressively we see 401/reconnect loops. Workarounds: 1) server-side token broker that issues short-lived session tokens to browsers and handles refresh; 2) resumable stream token that the server will accept with resumable_id+offset on reconnect. We have a resumable prototype (branch \"stream-resume\") that returns resumable_id on stream start.

tom: Sample resumable open: ```js
// initial open
const es = new EventSource(`/v1/chat/stream?resumable=true`, { headers:{ Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}` } });
// server returns a resumable_id in a control event
// on reconnect after 401: fetch('/session/renew') -> { token, resumable_id }
const es2 = new EventSource(`/v1/chat/stream?resumable_id=${resumable_id}`, { headers:{ Authorization: `Bearer ${newToken}` } });
```
Re-establishing with resumable_id avoids replaying full history and keeps demo smooth.

priya: Important compliance note: if you broker tokens server-side, document the broker as part of the data flow for SAML attestation. Also capture whether audit log exports to their SIEM are required.

maya: Known blocker: node/browser SDKs currently have a bug where SSE client auto-refresh isn't wired for resumable flows; reconnects can drop function_call state. Patch PR #1523 is in review to add resumable + credential auto-refresh. CI checks pending.

ci-bot: PR #1523 opened by @tom - \"sse-resume-credential-refresh\" (CI queued).

clarence: Will that block the demo?

tom: Not necessarily. For the demo recommend either A) use server token broker + resumable prototype today, or B) issue long-lived demo creds on a Dedicated trial to avoid rotation mid-session. We can cherry-pick PR #1523 into a canary if the demo wants hosted.

maya: Pricing note: ballpark hosted calc for bursts: assume avg request 70 prompt tokens + 130 response tokens = 200 tokens/request. For 1k QPS that's 200k tokens/s -> multiply by duration and hosted token unit cost. Dedicated reduces unit cost and gives latency SLOs (p50 ~100ms with quantized model + batch=1). I'll draft a one-pager with a spreadsheet.

priya: I'll start pre-filling the security questionnaire and list legal/BYOK lead time (~2-3 weeks typical). Also ask customer whether they need audit log exports or extended retention.

clarence: Customer contact is oliver@inverra.com. Can we get a one-page runbook covering: SSE example, websocket fallback, resumable pattern, function_call handling, schema validation, token-broker pattern, and a simple cost calc? Also include a fallback demo plan if PR #1523 isn't ready.

maya: On it. I'll include a sample quickstart repo and a hosted vs dedicated comparison.

tom: I'll prepare the resumable demo branch and try to get PR #1523 merged to canary.

priya: Tagging legal for LOA and KMS attestation items.

clarence: Thanks all. I'll schedule a Thurs demo with Inverra and include oliver@inverra.com. Tagging @maya @tom @priya for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
